Title: Panel-owned display-off executor
Requirement: The wall image shall execute a panel-authenticated display-off request through the existing local setup socket while WALL_ABSENCE_ENABLED remains false. The panel alone decides FULLSCREEN plus 30 seconds of observable absence; the image serializes the resulting verified backlight-off write with touch wake. Suspend remains the image's existing one-hour-and-schedule decision.
Rationale: The renderer owns display mode and derived presence; duplicating its timer in the image creates competing backlight writers. The image still owns privileged execution and scheduled suspend.
AcceptanceCriteria: Socket validation accepts only the empty conclusion shape and refuses wake evidence; the shell arm takes the power lock, verifies off, succeeds idempotently when already dark, and does not invoke occupancy or suspend. The existing decider proves suspend needs both the dark hour and schedule.

Title: Verified LCUS-2 amplifier actuator
Requirement: The wall image shall use the LCUS-2 amplifier actuator with one common bounded audio detector, and shall accept no other actuator: the audio-jack tone actuator, its trigger_out PCM and its WALL_AMP_TONE_HZ tuning are removed (Owner, 2026-09-13), the built-in jack is reserved for the item 23 headset leg, and a configuration naming any other activator shall fail loudly at firstboot and at service start rather than fall back. LCUS-2 shall own exactly one configured channel, use its measured 9600-baud command/status protocol through a stable CH340 device link, establish OFF before ON, verify every state and heartbeat, and establish verified OFF at service start, quiet transition, shutdown and before S3. Suspend shall be refused if OFF cannot be verified.
Rationale: The LCUS-2 retains relay state after its serial port closes, so process death or a green write exit cannot prove the amplifier is off. A stable udev link prevents enumeration order from selecting another serial device, and exact channel ownership preserves the unused relay.
AcceptanceCriteria: Unit tests assert that the Tone class and every tone symbol are absent, that audio-jack is refused with an error naming lcus-2, that no shipped configuration still declares trigger_out or WALL_AMP_TONE_HZ, and assert the four measured command bytes, exact two-line status parser, owned-channel sequence, heartbeat, retry/failure behavior, safe path/channel validation and backend-specific tools. Config tests assert LCUS-2 is the initial default and the VID 1a86/PID 7523 rule creates /dev/wall-amp-relay. Power-lifecycle tests prove failed OFF blocks S3 and successful resume restarts the detector. Physical evidence is limited to Windows COM4 enumeration, both audible channel clicks, exact status replies and state persistence across close/reopen; Linux enumeration and amplifier wiring remain physical acceptance.

Title: Offline bounded Door-motion image boundary
Requirement: The wall image shall carry python3-opencv through its offline apt closure and require doorstream/motion.py in the private application artifact. Motion shall default disabled and uncalibrated and become eligible only when both explicit booleans are true and every bounded numeric/zone/mask literal byte value validates; masks shall have explicit serialized-byte and rectangle-count ceilings. The unprivileged Door service shall receive only the camera and validated detector allowlist through RAM-backed systemd credentials, run with CPU/memory/task/stop ceilings, and be stopped before backlight-off or suspend. Runtime purge shall runtime-mask restart and use bounded stop/kill/reset plus a stable unit/account inactivity proof before unlinking credentials/socket. Tracked and SIM configuration shall contain no camera credential, image, or real-property zone.
Rationale: The application owns MOG2/tracking and the sanitized motion protocol, but those cannot work offline or remain safe through dark/suspend transitions unless the image supplies the dependency, configuration boundary and lifecycle enforcement. An uncalibrated full-frame default is not a detector policy; Door motion is explicitly forbidden from waking a dark panel. AWK escape reinterpretation and a momentarily absent process are not valid evidence for the bytes or lifecycle actually delivered.
AcceptanceCriteria: python3-opencv is named in packages.list and tested by importing cv2 and executing the artifact's motion.py inside the same clean Ubuntu package closure used for Electron. Capability validation requires doorstream/motion.py. Firstboot validates booleans exactly plus literal numeric, normalized trigger/road rectangle, and at most 32 mask values totaling at most 4096 ASCII bytes; escaped delimiters/punctuation are rejected. Invalid or uncalibrated configuration writes a false effective enable and makes provisioning red. Incomplete payload or camera input first runtime-masks restart, then performs bounded stop/kill/reset and requires both unit and dedicated-user inactivity throughout a settle interval before purging stale credentials/socket; inability to prove stable inactivity makes provisioning red without unlinking evidence. Fake lifecycle tests cover stop timeout, kill recovery, persistent activity and delayed restart. Unit ceilings are explicit. SIM remains disabled, uncalibrated, unreachable and topology-free. Physical detection quality/load is not claimed.

Title: Bounded panel-local Bluetooth/audio broker
Requirement: The wall image shall ship an off-by-default local Unix-socket audio broker with a fixed request protocol, pure route/trust policy, bounded visualizer telemetry, narrow root-only audio environment, killable backend execution, and crash-safe mutation state. It shall expose no TCP listener, shell command, arbitrary D-Bus call, raw audio, hardware address in any common textual form, or unreviewed automatic capture source. Until a real-panel probe establishes adapter roles, latency, coexistence, and PipeWire session ownership, the production backend shall route no device and shall report device routing unavailable, and mutation authorization shall ship denying every verb that names a device; the panel's own output switch, microphone button and level are not device routing and shall be served by writing one sequenced request for the root applier, refused as unavailable where that applier is not installed. The adapter's own power/discoverable/pairable policy and the A2DP sink are NOT governed here and are specified by SR-025; this requirement constrains only the renderer-facing broker, which remains off by default and grants no BlueZ authority. **AMENDED 2026-09-19 (Owner: "need bluetooth to have a method to trust a device, might need a method to either enter a PIN, set a number, or turn on discoverability"). The routed-device backend now ships and the clause that held it back is honoured rather than waived.** That clause forbade routing "until a real-panel probe establishes adapter roles, latency, coexistence and PipeWire session ownership"; what ships answers it by AVOIDING the question rather than by claiming to have settled it -- the broker still performs no device I/O and owns no BlueZ authority, and every device verb becomes one sequenced request for a root applier, exactly as the output switch already did. The wall image shall therefore additionally: manage Bluetooth devices from the panel through that applier (discover, a bounded discoverability window, pair with an optional passkey, trust and untrust, connect, disconnect, forget, and input/output route selection); name every device by a derived alias whose assignment is stable for as long as the device is seen and is never a hardware address in any textual form; report the pairing window and the passkey BlueZ produces so a person can compare it against the other device; and ARM this surface only where the applier is installed, denying every device verb at the authorization callback where it is not, so a request is never accepted into a file nothing will read. The routed output shall be a leg BESIDE the three-position switch and shall not become a fourth position of it. PipeWire session ownership remains unestablished and unclaimed: nothing here uses it.
Rationale: The Electron renderer needs one narrow capability rather than ambient control of bluetoothctl/wpctl. PipeWire is normally user-session state, while a separate service identity is desirable for BlueZ least privilege; choosing either without evidence can yield a broker that is secure but cannot route, or functional only through excessive authority. A mutation timeout is an uncertain side effect, not permission to replay it. Cooperative cancellation alone cannot reclaim capacity from an uncooperative backend. The 2026-09-12 decision to make the panel a Bluetooth speaker (SN-019) made the original blanket "no broad BlueZ policy" clause false, so the front door was split out rather than left contradicted by the image.
AcceptanceCriteria: Malformed, oversized, unknown, unauthorized, stale/unsafe-generation, untrusted-restore and implicit-input requests are refused. Backend operations run in bounded child processes; expiry terminates and reaps a child before returning capacity, including fifth-and-later recovery after repeated hangs. Mutations serialize without starving status/telemetry, persist intent before dispatch and result after success, deduplicate exact completed replay across restart, and leave every post-intent exception sticky uncertain. The Unix socket is mode 0660 and refuses a peer whose SO_PEERCRED UID differs from the configured service UID. Status and derived telemetry remain available with a mockable unavailable backend; results follow positive schemas and exclude colon/hyphen/underscore/compact/Cisco-dotted addresses including confirmation fields, BlueZ paths and raw or encoded audio. Route actions select only kind-correct trusted inventory aliases. Telemetry crosses IF-015 only as finite bounded bands/RMS/peak, active state, broker-owned generation and monotonic observation time; applies bounded cadence and silence hold; zero RMS stays silent at a zero floor; booleans and non-JavaScript-safe integers are refused; no sample buffer survives. Image configuration defaults disabled and physical radio/audio claims remain explicitly unproven. Device verbs are refused at the gate on a panel without the applier, and accepted into a per-sequence spool on one that has it; a spooled request is performed at most once across a replay, an applier restart and a backwards clock step, and a request the bound or a failed unlink leaves behind is picked up within the observer's period rather than stranded. An observer document that is absent, malformed, from the future or older than its shelf life reads as "do not know" and never as "no devices". No hardware address appears in the document the broker reads, in a request, or on IF-015 -- including a device whose own BlueZ name IS its address, which is substituted rather than allowed to fail the whole document. An alias is not reassigned to a different device while the first is still present. The published passkey is digits only, bounded in length, retires with its window, and cannot be carried from one window into the next.
Permutations: enabled={false,true}; request={valid,malformed,oversized,unknown}; authorization={allowed,denied}; backend={unavailable,mock,unsafe-result,hung,raises-after-effect}; peer={configured,mismatched}; socket-mode={0660}; device={trusted,untrusted,missing,wrong-kind,address-shaped,cisco-dotted}; input={explicit,implicit}; telemetry={unavailable,silence,zero-floor,signal,non-finite,oversized,over-cadence,backend-generation-mismatch}; generation={current,stale,unsafe,concurrent,restart,replay,uncertain}; applier={installed,absent}; device-verb={discover,cancel,set_discoverable,pair,trust,untrust,connect,disconnect,forget,select_input,select_output}; spool={empty,one,burst,over-bound,unconsumable}; document={fresh,absent,malformed,future,stale,duplicate-alias,address-shaped-name}; alias={new,retained,renamed,displaced,collided}; pairing={closed,open,passkey,expired,stale-from-previous-window}

Title: Zero-touch always-on stack
Requirement: The stack shall bring every service up unattended from an autoinstall image and self-heal on reboot/crash.
Rationale: Always-on infra must not need manual clicks (SN-001).
AcceptanceCriteria: autoinstall+first-boot start all services with no prompts; every service has restart:unless-stopped and a healthcheck; power-cycle returns all services within ~1 min on a Docker host.

Title: Split-horizon DNS + edge TLS + blocklists
Requirement: Technitium shall serve split-horizon A records to LAN_IP and Caddy shall obtain a public cert valid on-LAN, with ad-blocklists enabled.
Rationale: One box owns LAN name resolution and edge TLS (SN-002).
AcceptanceCriteria: provision-technitium.sh (idempotent) creates the zone, records, forwarders, and blocklists; dig against the box returns LAN_IP; https on-LAN shows no cert warning.

Title: Google-auth gate for the tracker
Requirement: The tracker subdomain shall be fronted by oauth2-proxy (Google provider) that admits only allow-listed accounts and forwards X-Forwarded-Email/-User to the tracker.
Rationale: Multi-user v1 needs real identity without a bespoke auth system (D1/D2/D3).
AcceptanceCriteria: oauth2-proxy config sets provider=google, an authenticated-emails allow-list, PASS_USER_HEADERS true, upstream=tracker:8787; a non-allow-listed account is rejected; verified on a Docker host.

Title: Tracker never directly reachable
Requirement: The tracker container shall be bridge-only (expose, not host-published) so its only ingress is via oauth2-proxy.
Rationale: Trusted headers are forgeable if the port is open (D2/WI-10.5).
AcceptanceCriteria: docker-compose.yml uses expose:8787 with no ports: mapping for tracker; Caddy routes the host to oauth2-proxy only.

Title: basic_auth retained for single-user services
Requirement: Caddy shall apply basic_auth to the actual and dns hosts and NOT to the tracker host.
Rationale: Only the multi-user tracker needs OAuth; keep the simple gate elsewhere (D2).
AcceptanceCriteria: Caddyfile imports protect_actual/protect_dns on those hosts; the tracker host has no basic_auth directive.

Title: Tracker image consumed as naglight:local
Requirement: Compose shall reference image naglight:local with a documented local build step and a commented build-from-sibling fallback; the migrated Dockerfile is reference-only. Dev boxes resolve locally-built images via a permissive chain: already present, else built from a sibling checkout, else pulled from a DECLARED public image knob (empty until the private app repo publishes), else a loud failure naming all three fixes.
Rationale: Q10.2 build-locally, no registry yet; NagLight owns the canonical build (D1/WI-10.4); NagLight/Finance-Auditor are PRIVATE, so a checkout must not be the only path once a public image exists.
AcceptanceCriteria: tracker service uses image naglight:${TRACKER_IMAGE_TAG}; README documents 'docker build -t naglight:local ../NagLight'; a commented build: fallback points at ../../NagLight; tracker/*.deprecated are clearly marked; scripts/ensure-local-images.sh implements the present->sibling->TRACKER_PUBLIC_IMAGE->fail chain and run-sim.sh invokes it.

Title: SSH key-only + Cockpit + unattended-upgrades
Requirement: Autoinstall shall enable SSH with key-only auth, install Cockpit reachable LAN-only, and enable unattended OS security upgrades.
Rationale: The headless box must be manageable over the LAN without physical visits (SN-005, KEY PIECE).
AcceptanceCriteria: user-data sets allow-pw:false with authorized-keys and a locked password; installs+enables cockpit.socket and unattended-upgrades; Cockpit is not proxied to the public internet.

Title: Remote ops workflow + reimage ladder memo
Requirement: The repo shall document the remote docker-compose workflow and deliver a reimage-over-LAN decision memo with checkboxes; nothing destructive is implemented without the Owner's ratification.
Rationale: Trivial remote debugging is a KEY PIECE; reimage is the HIGH-RISK line (only implement past a checkbox).
AcceptanceCriteria: REMOTE_MANAGEMENT.md covers SSH/compose/Cockpit ops and the reimage ladder (GRUB-reinstall / PXE-netboot / smart-plug+USB) with a recommendation and unchecked boxes; no destructive path is wired.

Title: Auxiliary LAN-only observability
Requirement: The stack shall include Uptime-Kuma and Dozzle (and optional self-hosted ntfy), LAN-only, health-checked, every knob in .env.example.
Rationale: Cheap operability for a self-hosted box (SN-006).
AcceptanceCriteria: compose blocks for uptime-kuma and dozzle (ntfy behind a profile) are bridge/LAN-only with healthchecks; every ${VAR} they use has an .env.example key.

Title: Public-facing, secret-free repo
Requirement: The repo shall track only *.example templates and gitignore all filled secrets/state; the local commit identity shall be diytechy, never the Owner's name/email.
Rationale: Q10.6 public-facing; WI-4.12 author-metadata lesson (SN-007).
AcceptanceCriteria: git config user.name=diytechy; .env/.token/allow-list/marker/user-data.filled gitignored; no real secret/hash/email/LAN-detail/personal-name in any tracked file.

Title: Honest config-level validation
Requirement: The check harness shall validate config coverage (env/Caddy/file + YAML parse) and the repo shall record, for every runtime claim, which validation tier proved it and what is still PENDING V3/hardware.
Rationale: Overclaiming runtime validation is a false green (SN-008). The no-Docker-on-the-dev-box premise was lifted 2026-07-03 (WI-10.13, WSL2 + docker-ce); the honesty bar was not, it moved to the sim/hardware boundary.
AcceptanceCriteria: scripts/validate_config.py passes: every ${VAR} in compose has an .env.example key, every Caddy {$VAR} is passed by the caddy service, referenced files exist, YAML parses; docs/status.md records what was NOT exercised.

Title: Opt-in tier-2 service catalog
Requirement: The stack shall define an opt-in catalog of self-hosted services (photos, video, music, podcasts, home automation, passwords, file sync, RSS/recipes/dashboard, update notifications) behind compose profiles — off by default, LAN_IP-bound or bridge-only, every knob in .env.example, images excluded from the baked ISO payload unless their profile is enabled at export.
Rationale: Use the box's headroom without endangering the validated core or bloating the ISO (SN-009); pins-never-drift needs an update NOTIFIER (diun), not an auto-updater.
AcceptanceCriteria: docker compose config lists no tier-2 service unless its profile is enabled; every tier-2 ${VAR} has an .env.example key; tier-2 ports bind LAN_IP or are bridge-only (Vaultwarden deliberately Caddy-only); export-images.sh without EXTRA_PROFILES bakes only the core+ntfy set; public exposure requires the three-step opt-in (profile + Caddyfile site + EXTRA_SUBDOMAINS record).

Title: Docker-volume sources in the backup table
Requirement: backup.sh shall accept volume:VOL[@CONTAINER] and path:/dir source specs in the single BACKUP_SOURCES table alongside //host/share, acquiring volume contents from the volume's mountpoint (docker volume inspect), optionally quiescing @CONTAINER (stop before copy, restart immediately after, EXIT-trap restart on any failure path), with every set then flowing unchanged through archive/hash/manifest/retention/report (no offsite step - the IceDrive client syncs chosen library paths directly; stack/backup/README step 5 is legacy/optional, Owner 2026-07-29).
Rationale: One table drives one execution sequence (Owner 2026-07-10); OI-8: the box's own volumes were backed up by nothing; a live DB copy needs an optional quiesce.
AcceptanceCriteria: Sim (mock-docker call contract + real pipeline): (a) a volume: set archives+hashes+restores byte-equal with zero stop/start calls; (b) volume:VOL@C issues stop before copy and start after, exactly once each, green run; (c) a forced mid-copy failure still restarts the container (EXIT trap) AND posts ok=false nonzero; (d) a cifs-only config makes zero docker calls; comment lines in the table are skipped.

Title: Host the Finance-Auditor pipeline
Requirement: The stack shall define a finance-auditor compose service per FA's IF-003 spec — profile-gated until FA's G-Final then promoted to core — with finance_snapshots + finance_actual_data volumes, FINANCE_* env knobs in .env.example, bridge-internal reachability to actual:5006 and tracker:8787, TZ-honored RUN_AT, and the image resolved via the SR-006 chain with --build-arg ACTUAL_API_VERSION pinned to ACTUAL_IMAGE_TAG; the snapshots volume shall be documented for LOCAL-only backup (never OFFSITE_SETS).
Rationale: FA is G3-complete and ships the image spec (its Dockerfile + DEC-19); the IF-002 pin coupling and the §3 privacy firewall are hosting-side obligations (SN-011).
AcceptanceCriteria: docker compose config lists finance-auditor only with its profile; every FINANCE_* ${VAR} has an .env.example key; ensure-local-images.sh builds finance-auditor:local with the ACTUAL_API_VERSION build-arg; backup.env.example carries the finance volume line with the never-offsite warning; no ports/healthcheck on the service (FA's documented design).

Title: Remote light UI for GUI-only vendor apps, shipped off and activated by HomeHub
Requirement: The repo shall provide a host-level setup script that installs xrdp plus a minimal XFCE session and the runtime libraries a GUI-only vendor app needs, plus a unit that creates a graphical session at boot with no client connected, so such an app runs unattended. It shall default OFF: the packages live in packages.optional.list (baked only when BAKE_OPTIONAL=1) and firstboot activates nothing unless REMOTE_UI_ENABLED=true and ICEDRIVE_MODE name it. Carriage and activation shall derive from a single declaration held by HomeHub, and a materialisation that activates a feature whose carriage is absent shall be refused.
Rationale: IceDrive's GUI client is the one app that needs this. A headless CLI exists and works, but it is a mount client rather than a sync client and is essentially undocumented by the vendor, so the Owner chose the supported client (2026-08-27). Carriage and activation were independent until then and disagreed for a month: eleven of the AppImage's runtime libraries were in no image at all, so the documented 'RDP in and sign in' step could not have been carried out on any hub ever built - and nothing reported it, because nothing had ever launched the app.
AcceptanceCriteria: packages.list carries 28 core names and none of the desktop or IceDrive set; packages.optional.list carries 22 (RDP/XFCE, the eleven Qt/xcb libraries the AppImage links against, and libfuse2t64) and export-apt.sh bakes them only when BAKE_OPTIONAL=1; .env.example ships REMOTE_UI_ENABLED=false and ICEDRIVE_MODE=off; firstboot step 6c activates nothing unless the knobs say so and itself refuses appimage-without-a-display; icedrive.pin pins both artifacts and export-icedrive.sh --artifact stages exactly one, writing artifact.kind so the payload destination is chosen by kind rather than by filename; HomeHub's Materialize-Deploy Test-ExtrasCarriage refuses an unknown mode, appimage without REMOTE_UI_ENABLED, and appimage with no pinned artifact; stack/remote-ui/README.md documents the LAN-only rule, the geometry/second-session hazard, and what does not self-heal.

Title: Wall-panel kiosk site (IP-gated identity injection)
Requirement: Caddy shall serve a wall kiosk site on {$WALL_HOST}:{$WALL_PORT} that is published bound to LAN_IP (never 0.0.0.0, and never router-forwarded), admits only {$PANEL_IP}/32 via remote_ip, serves the shell's static build as its document root AND reverse-proxies /api/* to tracker:8787 injecting X-Forwarded-User={$PANEL_USER_SUB} in place of any client-supplied identity header, and responds 403 to everything else.
Rationale: A keyboard-less panel cannot complete an interactive OAuth consent, so every session expiry would leave a Google login screen on the office wall (OI-12, ratified 2026-07-29, the LAN-port+/32 variant). This makes SR-004's premise gain a SECOND trusted-header injector, which is why it needed ratification; NagLight has no header HMAC in v1, so strip-before-set and a single-address match are the whole of the safety argument. Same-origin serving is a hard requirement, not a convenience: NagLight sends no CORS headers.
AcceptanceCriteria: V1 sim (validate-sim.sh checks 7-8): (a) a request carrying a FORGED X-Forwarded-User from the panel's /32 reaches the tracker as PANEL_USER_SUB, read back off /api/export's Content-Disposition; (b) the panel's /api/today is 200 and / serves the static build without swallowing /api/*; (c) the same requests from a NON-panel source address get 403 with Caddy's own body, proving refusal at the edge rather than at the tracker. Config: the Caddyfile carries no `bind` (LAN-binding is the compose publish) and no delete of the injected header (Caddy applies deletes AFTER sets). HARDWARE-ONLY REMAINDER: the off-LAN 403 from a real WAN vantage, and that Docker's port publish preserves the panel's source IP on the real box.

Title: Wall-panel image variant (graphical, config-only)
Requirement: The repo shall provide a SECOND autoinstall target for the wall panel — a graphical variant that boots into one fullscreen app under a Wayland kiosk compositor with no login, configures Wi-Fi from placeholders, applies the panel's hardware quirks as config, and implements a nightly sleep window with a guaranteed wake behind one knob — carrying no product source and leaving the AWOW variant (including its storage layout) untouched.
Rationale: The wall image overlaps this repo almost entirely at the image layer, so a second target is cheaper and safer than a second pipeline (D-W0). Its bar is NOT SN-001's zero-click always-on guarantee (OI-12b): the panel is a disposable thin client that is deliberately dark for part of the day, and a fix needing a value only the hardware can supply must be templated and named, not guessed.
AcceptanceCriteria: autoinstall/wall/user-data parses as cloud-config and installs cage + a tty1-autologin kiosk session, no Docker and no Cockpit; wall.env.example declares every knob a wall script reads (validate_config.py check 5) and the shipped template is all placeholders; wall-firstboot.sh is idempotent and non-interactive, writes the quirk-1 logind conf, masks iio-sensor-proxy (quirk 2), generates the quirk-3 udev rule ONLY when WALL_DISABLE_INPUT is set (and warns loudly otherwise, embedding the on-site re-enable one-liner), writes NM powersave-off + cloned-mac-address=permanent and renders netplan at 0600 (quirk 5), and renders the sleep-window timers from SLEEP_START/SLEEP_END; SLEEP_MODE=suspend arms the RTC alarm BEFORE suspending and refuses to suspend if it cannot; wall-wakeprep re-enables the ACPI USB wake source + USB device wakeup on every boot; mem_sleep_default=deep is reported, never silently written; WALL-BURN-IN.md enumerates the hardware-only remainders. NOT covered by any tier below hardware: the graphical session itself, Wi-Fi association, suspend/resume, and every quirk's real effect.

Title: Unified file-share and whole-library-backup feed
Requirement: The deployment shall publish one combined NagLight item whose share-health override is red when /srv/library is not mounted or a representative Samba read fails and whose normal band is based on whole days since the last artifact-verified FileBackup success. Share-health and last-success state shall be independent; only FileBackup advances last success.
Rationale: The prior library-mounted, backup-drive-mounted, backup and library-backup presentation lanes overdesigned the panel and allowed health probes to obscure backup freshness.
AcceptanceCriteria: One declared item/check contract exists. The monitor tests both mount and Samba, sets/clears only the health override, and never reports backup success. FileBackup advances last success only after artifact verification. A fault-to-recovery transition restores the pre-fault age band. Legacy per-drive items, feed ids and user-facing mount/identity/path details are absent from fresh provisioning; physical preflight and identity safeguards remain internal.
Permutations: mount=set{present,absent}; samba=set{available,unavailable}; last_success_days=range[0..3]; transition=set{startup,fault,recovery,verified-backup}; @pairwise plus recovery at each age boundary

Title: AI CLI service on the hub (contained, subscription-backed)
Requirement: The repo shall provide a plain hub service - no container - that accepts messages over HTTP from on-box callers and answers them by running one headless CLI session on the household subscription, with the model and the depth taken from a registry row rather than the request and the answer constrained by a supplied --json-schema. It shall run as a DEDICATED UNPRIVILEGED ACCOUNT that is never `hub`, restrain tool use to READ-ONLY with no --dangerously-* flag anywhere in the tree, BIND ONLY to loopback or the docker bridge and never the LAN, and give EACH REQUEST its own scratch working directory. It shall ship OFF, gated like REMOTE_UI_ENABLED, and declare no credential in the repo.
Rationale: A40 (ratified 2026-09-09) dropped the container: containment was the only reason to want one and it delivers none here, because the subscription credential must come from a home directory a human logged into interactively, so a container has to mount that home and the isolation is punctured at the only point that mattered. Containment therefore has to come from the account, the flags, the bind and the working directory - and ai-template's answers to the first two are wrong here, because that repo is itself the consented unattended run while this service's work is chosen by a caller. `hub` carries (ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL, so a caller-driven agent running as `hub` is arbitrary code execution as a passwordless-sudo user.
AcceptanceCriteria: tests/test_ai_cli_service.py and stack/ai-cli/tests/ai-cli-guards.test.sh assert each of the four properties against the SHIPPED artifacts, not fixtures: (a) the unit's User is neither hub nor root and assert_service_account refuses hub, root, a sudo/docker/adm group membership and any sudoers rule naming the account, while ignoring a commented rule and a similarly-named account; (b) a tree-wide git grep finds no --dangerously-* token, a copied ai-template row is REFUSED at startup and at every launch, the refusal is by prefix so a future flag is caught, --bare is refused because it needs an API key, and every shipped route carries its family's read-only tokens with the read tools still allowed; (c) resolve_bind accepts loopback and 172.16/12 and refuses the wildcard by name, a LAN address, a public address, a hostname and the empty string, and `--check` exits 2 on a LAN bind; (d) three consecutive requests get three distinct 0700 directories under the scratch root, the directory is removed on the raising path as well as the clean one, and the cwd the session runs in is that directory. Plus: the schema is required, the prompt rides stdin not argv at 40k chars, a request-supplied model or effort is ignored, and a zero exit with no result object is reported as a failure and cools the route.

Title: Occupancy-driven display power in the wall image
Requirement: The wall image shall derive the panel's backlight state AND its suspend/RTC-wake action from ONE evaluation of ONE knob set (SLEEP_MODE, SLEEP_START, SLEEP_END, WALL_ABSENCE_ENABLED, WALL_ABSENCE_TIMEOUT_MIN, WALL_PRESENCE_FILE). With WALL_ABSENCE_ENABLED=false it shall change nothing: the existing SLEEP_START=22:00 schedule stands unchanged and no presence is consulted. With it true: the backlight shall be off whenever nobody is present; the panel shall suspend only after WALL_ABSENCE_TIMEOUT_MIN of continuous absence OUTSIDE the on-period, arming the RTC wake for the on-period start; and it shall NEVER suspend inside the on-period, so a walk-in is a backlight write and not a resume. SLEEP_END shall be the single value that is the RTC wake target, the morning wake timer and the start of the on-period; its shipped DEFAULT is 06:45 (ratified 2026-09-08) on the occupancy path and the unchanged 06:30 on the schedule-only path, since the same acceptance promises the disabled path is untouched. The absence timeout shall measure absence spent OUTSIDE the on-period. The panel shall not suspend unless the RTC alarm has been READ BACK from the RTC after arming, and shall not suspend when the backlight could not be turned off. Absence shall be believed ONLY when a fresh, well-formed, correctly versioned presence signal positively asserts it; every other state - missing, unreadable, malformed, wrong version, stale, future-stamped, or unknown - shall read as PRESENT.
Rationale: SN-015 (ratified 2026-09-09) refines SN-013's 'sleeps overnight'. The defect this requirement exists to prevent is TWO parallel knob sets, one for the backlight and one for the suspend, that agree when written and drift afterwards - the symptoms being a dark screen on an awake machine, or a suspend with somebody standing at the panel. The fail-safe direction is asymmetric on purpose: a wrongly-lit panel is a nuisance, a wrongly-suspended one has NO LAN presence until the RTC fires and cannot be woken by its own I2C-HID touchscreen. The presence signal is a file rather than the sensor socket because that socket checks SO_PEERCRED against the panel uid and refuses root by design; the app senses, the image powers (IF-012).
AcceptanceCriteria: stack/autoinstall/wall/tests/occupancy-power.test.sh asserts the ARTIFACTS, never a timer's exit code, against the shipped wall-sleep.sh with a fake sysfs backlight tree and recording rtcwake/systemctl shims: the brightness file really contains 0; the epoch actually handed to rtcwake converts back to 06:45 and is in the future; a suspend was really recorded. Detection off writes neither half however long the absence, while the 22:00 start still suspends and still arms 06:45. Detection on: present inside the on-period leaves the screen lit with NO suspend ever recorded (the walk-in needs no resume); ten hours of absence inside the on-period dims but never suspends; 61 minutes outside it suspends and arms 06:45; 30 minutes outside it does not. SN-013 holds: an rtcwake that cannot arm refuses the suspend and degrades to backlight-off on BOTH paths, and a mains blip (an empty tmpfs absence clock) cannot suspend and restarts the clock from now. A missing, malformed or stale presence file leaves the panel lit and awake. An absence begun inside the on-period does not suspend at the boundary; a truncated absence clock does not read as decades of absence; a NaN observedAt is malformed rather than fresh; an rtcwake that exits 0 having programmed nothing does not count as armed; a backlight that cannot be turned off blocks the suspend; the alarm is armed with the frame the box reports and lands at the right local wall-clock time across a DST boundary. Structurally, exactly one file in the wall tree can change the backlight or suspend BY ANY MECHANISM, one tick invokes the decider exactly once (counted at runtime), and one SLEEP_END line drives both the on-period gate and the armed alarm in the same run. tests/test_wall_occupancy.py covers the decision truth table.
Permutations: absence_enabled=set{true,false}; presence=set{present,absent,unknown,missing,malformed,stale,future-stamped}; on_period=set{inside,outside}; absent_minutes=range[0..600]; sleep_mode=set{suspend,backlight}; rtc_arm=set{ok,refused}; absence_clock=set{present,lost-to-tmpfs}

Title: AI-usage feeder on the hub (profile-gated, one identity, never green on failure)
Requirement: The repo shall provide a plain hub service - no container - on a systemd timer that reads how much of each AI subscription has been consumed and POSTs it to NagLight as gauges. Three sources: Codex via `codex app-server` JSON-RPC `account/rateLimits/read`; Claude via the OAuth usage endpoint with its beta header and a `claude-code/<version>` user agent; OpenCode Go via GET https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/usage with a workspace bearer key. Gemini is OUT (deferred as E11). It shall NEVER WRITE A VENDOR CREDENTIAL FILE, shall post an UNAVAILABLE (stale) gauge and never a green one for any source that errors, times out, returns garbage or returns 401, shall be SCOPED TO ONE EXPLICIT IDENTITY in the manner of TRACKER_DRIVE_USER and REFUSE TO GUESS, and shall ship OFF. It sends NUMBERS ONLY and never a colour or a severity.
Rationale: Every parser was written against ONE REAL CALL made before it existed (2026-09-09), because a parser built from documentation posts fiction that looks exactly like a healthy subscription. The credential posture is A40's: these are INTERACTIVE subscription tokens minted by a human in an RDP session that do not survive a reimage, so a feeder that wrote one would cost a person a login, and a container would have to mount the home they live in - which is why this is a plain service. `observed_at` is when the value was TRUE, so a failing source reposting its last real reading at its original stamp goes stale on NagLight's own horizon: that is how 'unavailable' is expressed without inventing a number.
AcceptanceCriteria: tests/test_ai_usage_feeder.py asserts each property against the SHIPPED artifacts and against bodies captured verbatim from the real calls: (a) open_for_write refuses every path but the one state file and every known credential basename, and a whole cycle run inside a throwaway HOME holding all three vendor credential files leaves every byte under it unchanged and writes exactly one file, which contains no token; (b) six failure classes (transport, timeout, 401, garbage body, empty body, a bug in our own reader) each still POST a gauge and none of them is fresh by NagLight's horizon table, a failed source reposts the last true value at its ORIGINAL stamp, a first-ever failure posts a gauge with NO observed_at, and a future stamp is not fresh; (c) resolve_identity raises SystemExit on unset/blank/whitespace and the shipped .env.example ships AI_USAGE_USER blank, while resolve_feed_url refuses a LAN address, a public address, a hostname, a non-http scheme and the empty string; (d) .env.example ships AI_USAGE_ENABLED=false and every near-miss value reads as off. Plus the wire contract: value and target present, min/max both sent, direction emitted IF AND ONLY IF window is, no severity/css/colour field, and the shipped timer interval asserted to beat a quarter of the weekly staleness horizon.

Title: Weight gauge fed from a verified vendor source, with the goal resident in the user's definitions
Requirement: The hub shall post one body-weight gauge to NagLight's POST /api/feed under the gauge id `weight`, carrying unit `lb`, an explicit `value` and `target`, no `min`/`max` (so the tracker infers its agreed 50 lb range around the goal), no `window` and therefore no `direction`, and an RFC3339 `observed_at` that is the time the reading was TRUE; shall take the target line ONLY from the `target` field of one item in the user's own definitions files - the item located by the WEIGHT_ITEM_CATEGORY and WEIGHT_ITEM_ID knobs, which name a place and can never carry a number - shall REFUSE unless that item also declares `unit: lb`, converting nothing, and shall post NOTHING when no goal is declared; shall carry a stamp from the current cycle if and only if that cycle read the source successfully, reposting a prior reading at its ORIGINAL stamp on failure and posting value 0 with no `observed_at` when there is no history; shall never open any file for writing but its own state file and that file's .tmp sibling; and shall ship off, refusing a blank identity, a non-local feed destination and an unknown source name rather than defaulting any of them. NI_A1 (2026-09-14): the posted `value` shall be rounded to 0.1 lb, and the SAME rounding shall be applied to the reading stored in the state file, while the `target` - a number the person typed into their own definitions - shall never be rounded. NI_A2 (Owner ruling 2026-09-14, Q4-Q6: `sister column with a second value line, id weight-waist; height fetched from Google Health dataTypes/height by the weight feeder; waist entered as a hybrid free entry`): the hub shall ALSO post, gated OFF by default behind WEIGHT_WAIST_ENABLED, a second gauge under the id `weight-waist` - which must sort AFTER `weight` because NagLight orders gauges by id and the panel draws the first as the headline - carrying label `Waist/Ht`, the weight gauge's own icon `scale` (the panel's grouping key, so the two share one cell), unit `ratio`, EXPLICIT `min`/`max` of target -/+ 0.25 (`ratio` is not in NagLight's unitRangeSpan, so omitting them is a 400 - the exact opposite of the weight gauge's rule), `favourable: low`, no window and therefore no direction, a `value` of waist_in / height_in rounded to 0.001, and an `observed_at` that is the OLDER of the two measurements' stamps; shall read the height from the SAME Google Health v4 route with the data type segment swapped to `height` under the SAME scope the weight read already holds, so NO consent change is asked of the household, requiring the field `heightMeters` by exact name and REFUSING any other shape rather than converting it; shall read the waist from NagLight's own GET /api/today over the already-verified local destination - searching `items`, `undoable` and `catchups`, checking the row's declared `unit: in` and never converting, and taking the stamp from `lastEventAt` and never from the clock - rather than by mounting the tracker's event log, which would hand this service every household member's whole history; shall take the ratio target from the `target` of the item WEIGHT_WAIST_CATEGORY/WEIGHT_WAIST_ITEM_ID names, which is a waist goal IN INCHES divided by the height, falling back to the documented default 0.5 when no usable target is declared; shall cache both halves in its existing state file and re-post them at their ORIGINAL stamps so a transient failure does not delete the gauge; and shall post NOTHING for this gauge when either half is missing or the pair is implausible, there being no unavailable form of it.
Rationale: SN-016 names the weight feeder as one of the two profile-gated feeder services this hub carries; NagLight's SN-040 is the need it serves and owns the gauge contract. SN-040 ruled that a missing or stale source renders stale and never green, and that the goal lives in the user's definitions so it syncs like everything else. Both are properties of WHERE data comes from, not of how a bar is drawn, so both belong to the producer. The stamp rule is the whole of the first: NagLight already treats `observed_at` as when a value was true, so binding the stamp to whether this cycle actually read the source makes every failure class - absent token, transport error, timeout, 401, garbage body, a well-formed body with no weight in it, and a bug in our own reader - collapse to one path that cannot render green. The goal rule is the whole of the second: a goal on the hub would need an SSH session and a redeploy to change and would not travel with the person's tracker, so the definitions are the only home that satisfies the criterion. WHICH KEY INSIDE THE DEFINITIONS CHANGED ON 2026-09-09 BY OWNER RULING: a top-level `weight_goal_lb` does not survive Drive SHEET mode, which this household runs, because internal/defsheet regenerates each .md from a fixed item-column list and drops unknown columns, so the goal was erased by the first sync after any sheet edit; and Google Health v4 has no goal concept anywhere in its discovery document, so there is no vendor fallback. `target` and `unit` are already item columns that round-trip. The unit is CHECKED rather than assumed because 77 kg is 170 lb and 77 sits inside the 40..1000 lb plausibility band, so the band cannot catch a wrong unit - the failure would be a confident, plausible, wrong number about a person's body. A missing goal is a DIFFERENT refusal from a missing source because the target line IS the goal - inventing one would draw a 50 lb bar around a number nobody chose and colour a real body weight against it. The omitted min/max is deliberate: `lb` is the one unit NagLight infers a range for, and computing goal+/-25 in the producer would put a second range authority downstream of the one the household agreed.
AcceptanceCriteria: A cycle that reads the source posts the measured weight at the time it was measured, and NagLight renders it fresh only while it is inside the static 7-day horizon; a real reading older than that horizon is rendered stale even though this cycle read it. Each of six failure classes posts a body that NagLight would render stale, and a failed cycle leaves the state file byte-identical so the stored stamp cannot decay. With no history at all the posted body has value 0 and NO observed_at key. The goal is read from the `target` of the item WEIGHT_ITEM_CATEGORY/WEIGHT_ITEM_ID names in the user's definitions dir, and only when that item declares `unit: lb`; a target in any other unit, or with no unit, or in the prose body, or on two items, or in two files, or blank, non-numeric, non-finite or outside a 40..1000 lb sanity band, posts nothing; a file still declaring the superseded top-level `weight_goal_lb` is refused with a message naming where the number goes, and a file declaring both is refused rather than ranked; a cycle with every plausible goal-shaped environment knob set and no declaration in the definitions posts nothing. A built body carries no min, no max, no window, no direction and no colour, severity or css field, and its observed_at parses as RFC3339. open_for_write admits the state file and its .tmp only; a whole cycle inside a throwaway HOME holding a refresh-token file changes no byte under it and writes exactly one file containing no token. The knob is off for every value but a literal true. The live value 180.11766820504496 posts as 180.1 and is stored as 180.1; a target of 170.25 posts unrounded; 0.04 lb still fails the plausibility band after rounding to 0.0. With WEIGHT_WAIST_ENABLED unset no second gauge is posted and no extra call is made; with it true and both halves readable the posted body is exactly {kind,id,label,icon,unit,value,min,max,target,favourable,observed_at} with id `weight-waist`, min/max at target -/+ 0.25 and no window, direction, colour, severity or css. The height URL differs from the weight URL in exactly the dataTypes segment and exactly one scope constant exists in the module. A height body carrying heightCm, heightMillimeters or a bare number is refused and no value or Google user id reaches the message. A waist row is found in any of the three /api/today arrays; a row with unit cm, with no lastEventAt, or with a count outside 15..80 in is refused; an absent row is not a failure. A waist of 85 against a height of 70 is refused by the ratio band. Every failure class in the ratio half - SourceFailure, nothing logged, and a bug in our own reader - leaves the weight gauge posted first and unchanged. A cycle whose sources are all dead re-posts the cached ratio at its original stamp, and a cycle that changes nothing leaves the state file byte-identical.
Permutations: source=set{read ok,absent token,transport error,timeout,401,garbage body,no weight in body,reader bug}; history=set{none,fresh,inside horizon,past horizon}; goal=set{declared,absent,blank,two files,twice on one item,two items same id,prose body,out of band,unparseable,unit lb,unit kg,unit missing,legacy key only,legacy key and target}; stamp=set{now,past,past horizon,future,unparseable,absent}; destination=set{loopback,bridge,LAN,public,hostname,empty,non-http}; enabled=set{true,blank,True,yes,1}; @pairwise plus every goal and stamp value; ratio_enabled=set{unset,true,True,yes,1,blank}; height=set{read ok,empty history,absent dataPoints key,heightCm,heightMillimeters,bare number,two at one instant disagreeing,out of band,transport error,cached,none}; waist=set{in items,in undoable,in catchups,absent row,no count,unit in,unit cm,unit absent,no lastEventAt,count 0,count 335,cached,none}; waist_target=set{in inches,declared twice,unit cm,unit absent,absent,out of band}; @every height and waist value

Title: Bluetooth front door and A2DP sink
Requirement: The wall image shall keep the Bluetooth adapter neither discoverable nor pairable at rest and shall open both only inside a bounded pairing window that is opened deliberately and closes itself. A BlueZ pairing agent shall be registered as the DEFAULT agent for the window's duration only, and shall be stopped on every exit path; a window whose agent cannot be registered shall not open. Received audio shall be delivered to the ALSA default PCM as an A2DP sink only, never as a source, so that existing forwarding and amplifier detection carry it unchanged. The rendered policy shall refuse permanently-pairable operation and any configuration that advertises a panel which will refuse every pairing. A device bonded inside a window may reconnect and play afterwards without one, and the image shall provide an enumeration and a revocation for such bonds.
Rationale: A wall panel is an unattended radio in a room: BlueZ completes a Just Works pairing with no interaction whenever an adapter is pairable and an agent is registered, so both must be true only while a person is deliberately standing at the panel. With no pairing UI in the shell to display a passkey, the bounded window IS the consent, exactly as a speaker's pairing button is. Registering an agent is not the same as being the default agent, and a window that opens in front of no agent rejects the pairing it was opened for. Persistent bonding is the feature and the residual risk at once, so it must be revocable rather than merely documented. Delivering to the ALSA default PCM rather than a named card is what makes the amplifier follow Bluetooth without the detector knowing Bluetooth exists, and what keeps the sink obeying wall-audio-mode.
AcceptanceCriteria: Rendered policy defaults to powered, window pairing, not discoverable and not pairable at rest, with a window bounded at both ends; permanently-pairable and discoverable-but-unpairable configurations are refused, as are near-miss boolean and out-of-charset alias values. The pairing helper sets both BlueZ timeouts BEFORE either property is opened and aborts if either write is refused; it starts the agent before opening and stops it on success, failure and interrupt; an agent that exits immediately is treated as no agent. The agent calls RegisterAgent and RequestDefaultAgent and exits non-zero if either fails, and authorizes only audio service UUIDs. A window that cannot be verified closed powers the adapter down. The sink runs a2dp-sink only and plays to the ALSA default PCM with no card pinned; that PCM is a plug wrapping the fixed-rate mixer in both output modes, so a 44.1 kHz stream opens it. A wall-audio-mode change stops the sink before the shared-memory sweep and starts it after. Bonds are enumerable and revocable, and revocation validates its argument as a hardware address before it reaches any tool. Physical pairing, audibility and amplifier acceptance are not claimed.
Permutations: enabled={false,true}; pairing={off,window,always}; window={30,120,600,out-of-range,malformed}; at-rest={closed,discoverable}; agent={registers,register-fails,default-agent-fails,exits-early,unstartable}; capability={NoInputNoOutput,DisplayYesNo,invalid}; timeouts={both-set,discoverable-refused,pairable-refused}; close={verified,unverified}; service-uuid={audio,non-audio}; bond={absent,present,forgotten}; forget-arg={valid-mac,malformed,empty}; mode-switch={trigger-to-panel,panel-to-trigger}; sink-profile={a2dp-sink,a2dp-source}; stream-rate={44100,48000}

Title: Panel audio survives a USB re-enumeration
Requirement: The wall image shall bind the line-in passthrough, the kiosk loopback forwarder and the amplifier detector to the USB audio adapter as a device, not as a path, so that a port change or hub replug stops all three and starts them again without a human. The adapter shall be identified by a port-independent udev alias and addressed by ALSA card id. Every long-running alsaloop shall have a bounded recover loop that exits rather than retrying forever, and the amplifier detector shall reopen the relay device with a bounded retry. A panel whose adapter is absent shall leave the three units inactive without a restart loop and without delaying boot or the kiosk. When the amplifier-side hub itself enumerates with no downstream ports, the image shall re-enumerate that hub automatically, bounded to at most two authorized toggles per hub within a ten-minute window, acting only while the adapter's device unit is inactive AND the hub has no children, started by a udev add event rather than by a timer or a daemon, journalling every decision including the decisions to do nothing, and failing closed -- resetting nothing -- when the adapter's state cannot be established or when the record that bounds the toggles cannot be written.
Rationale: Measured 2026-09-13 (Owner item 25): after the hub moved ports the kernel re-enumerated the adapter with the same card id and udev recreated the relay symlink, but alsaloop kept a handle on the dead device instance and logged unable to prepare slave forever. alsaloop never exits on that path, so Restart=always never fires and the unit reads as active while no audio moves at all -- a failure with no red anywhere. The kernel device unit name embeds the USB port, which is the thing that changed, so only an alias can be depended on. Addendum measured 2026-09-13 21:52: on a second move the hub answered and none of its ports did (hub_ext_port_status failed, err = -71), so all of the above had nothing to recover onto; the whole mechanism depends on the hub cooperating. Toggling authorized is a hardware reset of everything downstream, the latching amplifier relay included, so the recovery is bounded and conditional rather than continuous.
AcceptanceCriteria: Unit tests assert the alias, the systemd tag set on every non-remove event, a SYSTEMD_WANTS for each of the three units, BindsTo=/After= on the alias in each unit, the guard as the single ExecStart of both alsaloop units, and the bounded relay reopen including its give-up. systemd-analyze verify passes on the three unit files where it is available. Unit tests additionally assert that the hub reset acts only on the 03eb:0902 device (not its interface and not another vendor), refuses any bus id that is not one before joining it to a sysfs path, never resets a hub that still has children, stops after two toggles in one run and after two within the cooling window across runs, and that the unit is a oneshot with Restart=no and no [Install]. Physical acceptance: with music playing, move the hub to another port; within 10 s the amplifier is on and kiosk audio is audible with no manual restart, and the journal shows each unit cycling exactly once. The hub reset's own acceptance is the journal of a real occurrence plus the non-destructive dry run in stack/panel-audio/README.md, because a hub that comes back empty is not reproducible on demand.
Permutations: event={add,change,remove,port-move}; adapter={present,absent-at-boot,late}; mode={trigger,panel}; alsaloop={healthy,wedged,intermittent}; relay={present,late,absent}; cap={under,over}; hub={healthy,empty,children-but-no-adapter,other-vendor,gone}; bus-id={valid,nested,malformed}; toggles={0,1,2,capped}

Title: Merged audio bus and the panel output switch
Requirement: The wall image shall provide a third output chain, `bus`, in which one stereo software bus carries the Bluetooth sink, the desktop S/PDIF capture and the kiosk player simultaneously, and a single switch selects mute, headset or speaker. Every direct plugin shall have a slave on exactly one card; clocks shall be joined by alsaloop forwarders. The amplifier detector shall read only a post-switch tap of the speaker leg, upstream of the volume control, and shall retain its unchanged hold-off. The switch shall be one host state file owned by a root applier, changed only through validated events, journaled on every change, and re-asserted after boot and after resume. The stored position shall survive a power cycle including the last setting, regardless of whether the headset adapter is plugged in over the boot. The headset adapter's USB presence, never a cable, shall flip speaker to headset once per plug, and only when the adapter is enumerated while the system is already running; headset selected with the adapter absent shall silence every output and report unavailable. Volume shall be one named control with per-output memory. The bus chain shall be additive: the trigger chain shall remain installed and selectable as a rollback. In the speaker position the leg shall open the adapter's eight-channel playback altsetting and shall carry the stereo bus to the front pair and an equal sum of both channels to both the centre and the low-frequency channels, through a per-channel trim table that is generated, adjustable without editing audio configuration syntax, and preserved across a re-provision. Where that chain cannot be opened the leg shall fall back to stereo front output and journal it, and an absent trim table shall not invalidate the rest of the audio configuration.
Rationale: Item 23 revision 2 with the Owner's rulings on its review. The adapter has one capture stream behind a four-way selector, so S/PDIF retires the analog line-in by construction; the headset adapter (0d8c:0014) reports no jack or mic insertion, so only its enumeration is observable; and a detector watching sources holds the amplifier on while the room is muted or the audio is in a headset. A plug-in is an event, and over a boot the panel cannot know when that event happened or whether it is still relevant, so coldplug presence is recorded and never acted on (Owner ruling 2026-09-13, after a power cycle returned the panel to Headset from Speaker). Placing the volume at the end of each leg rather than on the bus keeps a quiet room from dropping the amplifier, which a bus-level gain upstream of the tap would do. The adapter's eight-channel altsetting carries a fixed channel map, so the map is not negotiated and the trim is expressed as mix coefficients; those are per source as well as per channel, which the adapter's own eight hardware volumes are not, and the Owner ruled the level tuning a dedicated session after everything else is in, which is why the coefficients are movable at runtime and survive a re-provision. Boot-minute underruns measured on 2026-09-14 were first answered by ordering the leg after provisioning, which review found to be a first-boot deadlock -- nothing in the leg is started by a boot target, so provisioning itself starts it and would have waited on a job ordered behind its own; the answer is therefore a larger forwarder ring on the half that underran, at a stated and reversible cost of about twenty milliseconds on the speaker path.
AcceptanceCriteria: Policy tests cover every switch transition, the one-shot latch and its re-arming, per-output volume memory, clamping, corrupt-state fallback field by field, and refusal of every malformed event. The applier is driven for real in dry run: stops precede starts, the level is applied last, no leg runs while the headset is absent and both cards are muted, the headset card is resolved by USB id rather than by name, a request with a bad envelope, a stale sequence or a presence claim is refused, and outside bus mode the state is recorded with no hardware command issued. Configuration tests assert one card per direct plugin, the three sources reaching one bus, the capture selector on IEC958 In, the detector's sole bus-mode source being the post-switch tap and the absence of any mode branch in the actuator, the softvol on the always-present loopback card, both udev aliases, no leg enabled, the boot and resume install targets, the presence unit ordered after the boot unit, the absence of any dependency on udev settle, the sysfs card number rather than the ALSA id as the thing that is dated, and trigger mode left intact. A coldplug presence report is asserted to record the adapter, set the latch and leave every position standing, while a runtime add still switches once. The speaker leg's eight-channel open, the identical sum reaching both the centre and the low-frequency channels, stereo surviving on the front pair, explicit zeros on the pair wired to a desktop input, every refusal of the trim command, field-by-field fallback of a damaged trim file, the single probe that precedes any open of the leg and is absent in the silent positions, and the ordering chosen against the boot-minute underruns are each asserted; and the generated configuration is parsed by the audio library itself, once with the trim table present and once with it removed, to prove that its absence costs only the centre and sub. No claim is made about audibility, lip-sync or amplifier wiring: those are the on-glass acceptance.
Permutations: output={mute,headset,speaker}; headset={present,absent,arriving,leaving}; latch={armed,spent}; mode={trigger,panel,bus}; request={valid,stale-seq,bad-envelope,presence-claim,malformed}; state-file={valid,missing,corrupt,partial}; volume={0,mid,100,under,over}; leg={running,stopped}; boot={cold,resume}; presence={coldplug,runtime-plug,unattributable}; speaker-chain={multi,stereo-fallback}; trim={default,moved-by-group,moved-per-channel,negative,over-ceiling,non-numeric,unknown-channel}; trim-file={present,absent,partial,corrupt}

Title: Panel microphone legs to the desktop input and the Bluetooth mic return
Requirement: The wall image shall, in the bus output chain, route one selected microphone to the 5.1 adapter's rear output and to a connected phone's HFP mic return. The selection shall follow the output switch: the panel's built-in capture in the speaker and mute positions, and the USB headset adapter's capture in the headset position. The input mute shall be a control separate from the output switch and shall be applied as a real mute -- every mic forwarder stopped and every available capture switch closed -- never as a presentation flag over a running microphone. With the headset position selected and its adapter absent, no microphone shall be routed anywhere. The microphone shall reach only the rear channel pair, and the merged bus shall reach only the front, centre and low-frequency channels; each route shall write an explicit zero into every channel it does not own, and the two shall share one direct mixing plugin over the adapter's single playback stream. The rear channels' hardware level shall be raised only while a mic leg is running and returned to silence otherwise. The capture gain shall be a generated, runtime-adjustable value preserved across a re-provision, not a hand edit. The microphone source shall be reachable under exactly one configuration name, so that an echo canceller can be inserted in front of every consumer in one line. No mic leg shall be enabled at boot, and no mic leg's failure shall fail an apply that carries the room's audio.
Rationale: Item 23 revision 2 spec C with D3 and D4, and Owner ruling E, which answered 'does the output Mute also mute the microphone' with 'no, the mic has its own mute' -- SUPERSEDED 2026-09-14 by Owner item J (SN-030): selecting output Mute also mutes microphone transmission, latched in wall_audio_state.normalize() for every caller including the physical rocker and boot state recovery, and leaving Mute does not unmute the microphone until an explicit microphone-unmute action. Three measurements shape it. The 5.1 adapter has one capture stream and bus mode spends it on the desktop's S/PDIF, so a wired microphone cannot share it and the sources are the built-in codec and the hot-plug headset adapter. The adapter's playback mute is a single boolean over all eight channels, so it cannot silence the front while the rear carries a microphone; the separation is therefore two generated route tables of explicit zeros over one shared direct mixing plugin, and the remaining hardware guarantee is the amplifier relay opening after its ordinary hold-off. The built-in microphone was found clipping at the level it had been left at, so the seeded capture gain is the measured level rather than a preference. A microphone's state cannot be heard from the room, which is why the mute stops forwarders rather than flagging them, why the selected source is journaled on every apply, and why a selected-but-absent headset tunnels nothing rather than falling back to the microphone in the room. Owner ruling 7 is the authority for that last point.
AcceptanceCriteria: Policy tests cover the source selection in every switch position, the input mute stopping both legs while leaving the output legs running, the output Mute position ALSO muting the microphone (item J) and refusing an independent unmute while it is selected, and a selected-but-absent headset routing nothing at all. Generated-file tests assert the microphone on the rear pair only, an explicit zero on every other channel, the complementary zeros in the speaker route, and that the two tables' owned channels are disjoint and together cover the whole map. Applier tests assert that only the rear pair of the adapter's eight hardware levels is moved and that an unreadable control moves nothing, that the rear level returns to silence when no leg runs, that a changed selection restarts the legs rather than starting them, that a mic leg's failure does not fail the apply while an output leg's does, and that the leg is refused while the speaker chain has fallen back to its exclusive stereo open. Knob tests assert refusal rather than clamping, that a refused value in a command moves nothing at all, and field-by-field fallback of a damaged file. Supervisor tests assert that only a synchronous-connection playback endpoint counts as a call, that a call in progress is never moved to another device, that an unreachable daemon means no call rather than an open microphone, that the poll interval is clamped, and that a rollback out of bus mode stops the leg. Configuration is parsed by alsa-lib itself: every name resolves, and removing either generated file costs only that file's name. Unit tests assert no mic leg is enabled and both carry the mode gate.
Permutations: source={panel,headset}; output={mute,headset,speaker}; input_mute={on,off}; headset={present,absent}; speaker-chain={multi,stereo}; sco={absent,one,two,lost}; mic-file={present,absent,damaged}; knob={in-range,out-of-range,unknown,malformed}

Title: Panel presentation and thermal telemetry collector
Requirement: The wall image shall run a local collector that samples, on a monotonic five-second schedule with UTC timestamps, every readable thermal zone and hwmon sensor it inventoried, whole-system CPU utilisation derived from counter deltas, and the renderer's own validated presentation snapshot (FULL or TABBED, selected tab, actual fullscreen owner, selected media preference, actual visualiser status, display power and music activity). It shall write a versioned JSONL schema carrying units, session and boot identifiers, rotate it under a seven-day retention and a 50 MiB hard cap, and expose a documented local export. A missing sensor shall be recorded as unavailable and never as zero; an initial CPU sample with no valid delta shall be unknown; a stale or absent renderer report shall be unknown and never logged as the current mode. Sampling or logging failure shall not block input, audio or rendering, and the collector shall not wake a suspended panel but shall identify the gap on resume. The renderer's snapshot shall be written to a run directory the unprivileged panel user can actually write.
Rationale: Plan item S. The panel's heat behaviour is the open question that gates the item Q ProjectM trial, and the trial is only meaningful if the log distinguishes the mode that was ACTUALLY on the glass from the remembered tab and the requested preference. The renderer snapshot moved to /run/wall-panel-renderer because /run/wall-panel is root-owned 0755 and the panel user could not write into it, which made the whole path fail silently; the application payload and the system payload must therefore ship together.
AcceptanceCriteria: Unit tests cover the sampler's counter-delta arithmetic, the unknown-until-a-valid-delta rule, unavailable sensors, alternate labels for one sensor not being double counted, rotation and the size cap, a clock jump, and a suspend/resume gap. Install tests assert the unit file is staged, installed, daemon-reloaded, enabled and started by firstboot, and that the tmpfiles fragment creates the renderer run directory with an owner the panel user can write as. Records are shown to differentiate Tabbed/Pandora from Fullscreen/Door and to carry mode-change entries for transitions shorter than one sample interval.
Permutations: sensors={present,absent,duplicate-label}; cpu-sample={first,delta,counter-reset}; renderer={fresh,stale,absent}; disk={ok,full}; lifecycle={start,restart,suspend,resume}; retention={under-cap,over-cap,over-age}

Title: ProjectM preset payload as a declared deployment dependency
Requirement: Where the opt-in ProjectM ambient visualiser is offered, the wall image shall carry its preset set as a hash-pinned payload reproduced from a committed lock file, install it to a documented location with recorded ownership and modes, and declare it in the release dependency manifest. A payload whose locked entries are absent or whose hashes mismatch shall fail the build and refuse the deployment rather than install partially. An EMPTY lock shall be reported as the deliberate unruled state -- no preset pack has been licensed and chosen by the Owner -- and shall not be presented as a successful install.
Rationale: Plan item Q. The upstream Milkdrop packs carry no licence, so the set is an open Owner ruling and the lock ships empty on purpose; the renderer is built to run presetless. The requirement exists so that the day a set is ruled in, the payload has a declared install transaction instead of a README claiming an installed location that nothing creates -- the state this row was written to correct (terra 2026-09-14, finding 5).
AcceptanceCriteria: The builder reproduces every locked file by SHA-256 or fails hard; an empty lock exits with the deliberate-state message and installs nothing. Install tests assert that a non-empty payload reaches the documented location with the recorded owner and modes and is named in the manifest, and that a removed or mismatched file is detected and refuses activation rather than being ignored.

Title: Responsive grid-stepped rocker with guarded apply
Requirement: The wall image shall move the physical-rocker volume by exactly one five-percent step per firmware break pulse, shall publish a bounded read-only absolute preview of the gesture that advances with those pulses and terminates explicitly, and shall apply each movement as an absolute compare-and-set against the audio mode, output, level and state revision it was computed on.
Rationale: Owner ratification 2026-09-16 (end-of-gesture rounding visibly took levels back) as amended 2026-09-18 by the strategy B selection: the 2026-09-18 kprobe capture at serio_interrupt proved the ~106 ms repeat is the firmware re-sending make/break pairs, so there is no held-duration to integrate and the pulse count is the specification. One apply costs 498-551 ms, so the overlay and the audible level must be driven by separate, bounded mechanisms rather than by one blocking loop.
AcceptanceCriteria: Tests cover one/many/reversed pulses, the gap adding no step, boundary clamping and pulse conservation (98 up down = 95), the exact preview schema and every terminal phase, a guard refusal after an output or state-revision change, an ambiguous verdict, and a bound of one active request plus one replaceable target.

Title: Per-connection volume-apply health
Requirement: The wall image shall report each wall-volume-request@ instance's exit status from the request apply, not from delivery of its verdict to a local peer. A peer that closes before sending a request shall make no change, journal one line and exit zero; once a request has been read, an undeliverable verdict shall preserve the apply result; and an unreadable partial request shall still fail. The request parser contract is unchanged: handle_request(b'') continues to return error and applies nothing. The template unit shall collect inactive and failed spent instances.
Rationale: A per-connection unit red solely because its reply peer left makes systemctl --failed unreadable and hides real failures. This is deliberately not a widened request boundary: EOF before a request is a transport no-op, whereas an empty request delivered to the parser remains invalid.
AcceptanceCriteria: tests/test_panel_volume_keys.py:test_connect_and_close_is_not_a_failure_sr028, test_an_undeliverable_verdict_reports_the_apply_not_the_delivery_sr028, test_an_undeliverable_verdict_still_reports_a_failed_apply_sr028, test_a_request_that_cannot_be_read_is_still_a_failure_sr028 and test_spent_instances_collect_themselves_sr028 prove the five outcomes. The unit declares CollectMode=inactive-or-failed.

Title: Capability-led weekly filesystem trim
Requirement: The hub shall replace the stock weekly fstrim command with a wrapper that enumerates real mountpoints, deduplicates them by source and consults each source device's advertised DISC-MAX capability. A source advertising DISC-MAX 0 is skipped with a printed reason; an absent or unparseable DISC-MAX answer is treated as no discard support and skipped with a printed reason; every other source is trimmed with stock fstrim options; an empty real-mount list succeeds; and a trim failure on an advertised-capable device exits non-zero. The fstrim.service drop-in shall reset ExecStart before adding the wrapper so the stock and wrapper commands cannot both run.
Rationale: /srv/library and /mnt/backup-drive are non-discarding spinning USB disks, but path exclusions would fail on a future mount layout. DISC-MAX is the device's own answer. systemd ExecStart is list-valued, so a drop-in without an empty reset silently retains the failing stock command.
AcceptanceCriteria: tests/test_homehub_fstrim.py:test_a_clean_run_trims_the_discardable_and_skips_the_rest, test_a_skip_is_never_silent, test_a_device_that_advertises_discard_and_then_refuses_is_still_a_failure, test_one_device_is_asked_once_however_many_times_it_is_mounted, test_a_device_lsblk_cannot_describe_is_skipped_rather_than_assumed and test_nothing_mounted_is_not_a_failure prove the wrapper outcomes and staged drop-in reset.

Title: Desktop S/PDIF retry preserves systemd start-limit protection
Requirement: The wall image shall configure wall-spdif-in.service with a bounded geometric restart delay for its external desktop S/PDIF capture source: it shall retain Restart=always and the existing StartLimitIntervalSec and StartLimitBurst, begin retrying at two seconds, progress through six restart steps and cap the delay at 120 seconds. The schedule derived from the unit's own values shall permit fewer starts than StartLimitBurst inside StartLimitIntervalSec, so a temporarily absent desktop clock cannot exhaust the limit while a genuinely hard-failing unit remains protected.
Rationale: S/PDIF capture opens only while the desktop source supplies a clock. Its temporary absence is normal during desktop sleep or idle output, while a panel-local leg failing to open is not established as the same condition. The 2026-09-15 flat retry hit the start limit; the desktop awake on 2026-09-16 opened cleanly.
AcceptanceCriteria: tests/test_wall_audio_switch.py::test_the_desktop_leg_backs_off_instead_of_exhausting_its_start_limit_sr028 derives systemd's schedule from wall-spdif-in.service and proves fewer starts fit in the configured interval than the configured burst limit. It does not freeze implementation constants beyond the requirement's stated policy.

Title: USB audio and relay re-enumeration recovery
Requirement: The wall image shall recover the configured audio switch and LCUS-2 amplifier actuation when the 0d8c:0102 adapter or 1a86:7523 relay re-enumerates. The adapter udev rule shall directly activate only non-switch-policy consumers and shall invoke one non-RemainAfterExit reassert of apply-state for all switch-dependent legs. apply-state shall log and succeed without issuing mixer or unit commands when the configured adapter is absent, but shall preserve failure reporting when it is present. The relay shall have a stable systemd alias and add activation; the actuator service shall want and order after that alias without binding its lifecycle to it.
Rationale: A manually maintained udev leg list already omitted bus-mode legs once, and the boot applier waited 45 seconds for hardware that appeared twenty seconds later. The relay is a separate actuator: its absence must be visible and recoverable but must not stop the audio graph.
AcceptanceCriteria: tests/test_wall_audio_reenumeration.py derives every adapter BindsTo unit from unit files and requires direct udev activation or policy.ALL_LEGS ownership; it also inspects the non-sticky reassert and relay alias/order. tests/test_wall_audio_switch.py exercises absent-adapter apply-state as a successful deferral.

Title: Removable audio hardware defers deployment without hiding switch or daemon failures
Requirement: The wall image shall treat an absent configured USB audio adapter as a deferred wall-audio-mode apply: it shall publish a consistent requested mode file and selected ALSA-chain symlink, issue no mixer or unit commands, log the deferral and exit zero. Publishing the selection is a precondition of the deferral, not an accompaniment to it: if the pair cannot be published the command shall restore the previous selection and exit non-zero, and shall report a failed restoration distinctly, because a symlink and mode file naming different modes is the one state no later reader can reconcile. A present-adapter mode switch that records any operation failure shall remain non-zero. When panel-amp-trigger receives SIGTERM or SIGINT after it has started, it shall attempt to record a safe relay OFF and exit zero only when the relay device node is absent; an unverified OFF against a PRESENT relay shall remain non-zero, as shall configuration and unsafe-start failures before a termination request.
Rationale: A removable device being out is normal during wiring and re-add policy already recovers it. A failure after the graph has begun changing is different: its half-applied warning prevents two chains driving one adapter. A BindsTo stop is likewise intended systemd lifecycle, not evidence that the relay daemon independently failed.
AcceptanceCriteria: tests/test_wall_audio_mode_selection.py EXECUTES set_mode_selection and require_mode_selection against a temporary tree, forcing publish and rollback failures, and is mutation-checked against both; tests/test_wall_audio_switch.py holds the deferred branch to the checked call and the retained fatal counted-failure path. tests/test_wall_amp_trigger.py drives SIGTERM through the relay-absent running loop and separately proves unsafe startup stays fatal. TC-953 remains a panel firstboot demonstration because no hermetic firstboot harness exists.
